headline: LinkedIn spent $5,249 over 14 days with zero conversions and is paused; Meta CPA is up 2.4x and is cut 30%; the direct surge looks AI-driven, not paid-driven.

moves.reason: 14 days, $5,249 spend, 0 conversions; daily spend climbed from ~$290 to ~$423 (+46%). Before that, CPA was ~$185 (ROAS 1.02). Self-reported LinkedIn share fell to 0% in the last 2 weeks. All attribution models put its CPA at $93-197. Pause is cheap to reverse.

Spend flat (~$3.5k/wk) but CPA rose from ~$58 (Aug-Sep) to $130-156 over the last 3 weeks; ROAS 3.1 to 1.3. Self-reported Instagram/Facebook share fell 18% to 6%, so the decline is corroborated and not just a tracking artifact. Even the most favorable model (first-touch) gives CPA $46, well above search at $17-33. Partial cut (-30%) rather than pause because the models still credit Meta 14-22% of conversions.

tests.hypothesis: Google Search is credited 39% (first-touch) to 69% (last-touch) of conversions, so its true incremental share is unknown. Part of its last-click credit may be capturing buyers sent by AI assistants or other channels.
tests.design: Geo split holdout: pause non-brand and brand search in ~20% of matched regions for 3-4 weeks, with the rest unchanged. Measure total conversions (all sources, including direct) per region, plus self-reported 'Google' share. Pre-register the lift threshold. Do not scale search before the result.

tests.hypothesis: Email gets 5% of credit under last-touch but 22% under first-touch (CPA $3.65-$16.74). It may be much more valuable than reported, and it is cheap at $40/day.
tests.design: Randomly hold out 10% of the email list for 4 weeks. Compare conversion rate and revenue per recipient between held-out and mailed groups, including conversions with no tracked source.

flag_verdicts.reason: Zero conversions for 14 days on $5,249, while daily spend rose from ~$290 to ~$423. Self-reported LinkedIn is 0% in the last 2 weeks. Paused.
Meta CPA went from ~$58 to $130-156 on flat spend. Self-reported Instagram/Facebook share fell 18% to 6%, which corroborates a real decline. Budget cut from $500 to $350/day.
Search spend spike of 1.7x the median on 9/12-9/18 held CPA at $23.58 vs $19.34. The latest week's CPA is $17.13, in line with the prior 4-week average of $16.94. No action needed.

Direct rose from 1.8 to 7.6/day (4.2x) while paid spend moved 1.03x. Self-reported AI answers rose from 7% to 23%. Paid channels should not get credit for this, so there is no budget move. Keep monitoring.

flags.message: linkedin spent $5,249 over 14 days with zero conversions, and spend is still rising.
meta CPA rose 2.4x, from $63 to $148, starting 2026-10-09.
google_search spend jumped for 7 days (2026-09-12 to 2026-09-18); CPA held at $24 vs $19. Likely fine, confirm before acting.
Direct conversions grew 4.2x (1.8 to 7.6/day) while paid spend moved 1.03x. Self-reported AI answers went from 7% to 23%. Something untracked is driving buyers.
